name: BancaAurora Risk&CMDB Analyst
description: Banca Aurora chatbot analyzer. Use the Knowledge Graph Layer to provide contextual and accurate answers. The data is recovered using the tools defined, using predefined parametric Cypher queries, similarity search on text embeddings using the neo4j vector index, and Text2Cypher
system_prompt:
You are a read-only graph analyst for Banca Aurora.
Your job is to explain business impact, technical exposure, remediation evidence, ownership and infrastructure reachability using the Neo4j graph.

Always prefer Cypher Template tools over Text2Cypher.
Use Similarity Search only for fuzzy or semantic security questions.
Use Text2Cypher only when no template tool can answer the question.

Never return embeddings, raw node objects, raw relationships, or element IDs.
Prefer concise business-first answers:
1. impacted business process
2. impacted application or repository
3. security signal (SAST, library CVE, runtime CVE)
4. infrastructure/server context
5. owner and recommended next investigation step

When a question is ambiguous, ask a short clarifying question.
When multiple assets are returned, rank them by business importance and risk.

tools.name: Natural Language to Cypher Tool
tools.description: A general-purpose, free-form Text-to-Cypher tool that converts natural language questions into Cypher queries, executes them, and returns the results. Use this option when no specialized tool (e.g. for aggregation or domain-specific logic) is more appropriate.

tools.name: business_process_risk_profile
tools.description:
Use for questions about one named BusinessProcess.
Returns the operating model, owning person, supporting applications, repositories, security findings, runtime context and a synthetic risk score.
Use when the user asks about the risk, dependencies, or technical footprint of a business process.
Parameter process_name must exactly match BusinessProcess.name.

config.template:
MATCH (bp:BusinessProcess {name: $process_name})
OPTIONAL MATCH (bp)<-[:OWNS]-(bpOwner:Owner)
OPTIONAL MATCH (bp)-[:CALLS]->(act:Activity)-[:USES]->(app:Application)
OPTIONAL MATCH (app)<-[:OWNS]-(appOwner:Owner)
OPTIONAL MATCH (app)-[:HAS_REPO]->(repo:Repository)
OPTIONAL MATCH (repo)-[:CONTAINS]->(si:SastIssue)
OPTIONAL MATCH (repo)-[:CONTAINS]->(:File)-[:IMPORTS]->(:Library)<-[:AFFECTS]-(libCve:CVE)
OPTIONAL MATCH (app)-[:RUNNING_ON]->(sw:Software)<-[:AFFECTS]-(runtimeCve1:CVE)
OPTIONAL MATCH (app)-[:RUNNING_ON*1..3]->(srv:Server)<-[:RUNNING_ON]-(runtimeSw:Software)<-[:AFFECTS]-(runtimeCve2:CVE)
WITH bp, bpOwner,
     collect(DISTINCT act.name) AS activities,
     collect(DISTINCT app.name) AS applications,
     collect(DISTINCT appOwner.name) AS applicationOwners,
     collect(DISTINCT repo.name) AS repositories,
     count(DISTINCT si) AS sastCount,
     count(DISTINCT libCve) AS libraryCveCount,
     count(DISTINCT runtimeCve1) + count(DISTINCT runtimeCve2) AS runtimeCveCount,
     collect(DISTINCT srv.name) AS servers
RETURN bp.name AS businessProcess,
       bp.revenue AS revenue,
       bpOwner.name AS owner,
       activities,
       applications,
       applicationOwners,
       repositories,
       servers,
       sastCount,
       libraryCveCount,
       runtimeCveCount,
       (sastCount + (2 * libraryCveCount) + (2 * runtimeCveCount)) AS riskScore
LIMIT 10

tools.name: application_security_profile
tools.description:
Use for questions about one named Application.
Returns business context, owner, repositories, SAST findings, vulnerable libraries, runtime software, runtime CVEs and hosting servers.
Use when the user asks what is risky about an application or how an application is exposed.
Parameter application_name must exactly match Application.name.

config.template:
MATCH (app:Application {name: $application_name})
OPTIONAL MATCH (app)<-[:OWNS]-(appOwner:Owner)
OPTIONAL MATCH (app)<-[:USES]-(act:Activity)<-[:CALLS]-(bp:BusinessProcess)
OPTIONAL MATCH (app)-[:HAS_REPO]->(repo:Repository)
OPTIONAL MATCH (repo)-[:CONTAINS]->(si:SastIssue)
OPTIONAL MATCH (repo)-[:CONTAINS]->(:File)-[:IMPORTS]->(lib:Library)<-[:AFFECTS]-(libCve:CVE)
OPTIONAL MATCH (app)-[:RUNNING_ON]->(sw:Software)<-[:AFFECTS]-(runtimeCve1:CVE)
OPTIONAL MATCH (app)-[:RUNNING_ON*1..3]->(srv:Server)
OPTIONAL MATCH (srv)<-[:RUNNING_ON]-(runtimeSw:Software)<-[:AFFECTS]-(runtimeCve2:CVE)
WITH app, appOwner,
     collect(DISTINCT bp.name) AS businessProcesses,
     collect(DISTINCT act.name) AS activities,
     collect(DISTINCT repo.name) AS repositories,
     collect(DISTINCT si.name) AS sastIssues,
     collect(DISTINCT lib.name + ' ' + lib.version + ' [' + libCve.cve_code + ']') AS vulnerableLibraries,
     collect(DISTINCT runtimeSw.name + ' ' + runtimeSw.version + ' [' + runtimeCve2.cve_code + ']') +
     collect(DISTINCT sw.name + ' ' + sw.version + ' [' + runtimeCve1.cve_code + ']') AS runtimeFindings,
     collect(DISTINCT srv.name) AS servers
RETURN app.name AS application,
       appOwner.name AS owner,
       [x IN businessProcesses WHERE x IS NOT NULL] AS businessProcesses,
       [x IN activities WHERE x IS NOT NULL] AS activities,
       [x IN repositories WHERE x IS NOT NULL] AS repositories,
       [x IN sastIssues WHERE x IS NOT NULL] AS sastIssues,
       [x IN vulnerableLibraries WHERE x IS NOT NULL] AS vulnerableLibraries,
       [x IN runtimeFindings WHERE x IS NOT NULL] AS runtimeFindings,
       [x IN servers WHERE x IS NOT NULL] AS servers
LIMIT 10

tools.name: repository_remediation_evidence
tools.description:
Use for questions about one named Repository and its remediation history.
Returns the application, owner, SAST findings, remediation commits and changed files.
Use when the user asks what was fixed, which findings were remediated, or how code changes relate to security issues.
Parameter repository_name must exactly match Repository.name.

config.template:
MATCH (repo:Repository {name: $repository_name})
OPTIONAL MATCH (repo)<-[:HAS_REPO]-(app:Application)<-[:OWNS]-(owner:Owner)
OPTIONAL MATCH (repo)-[:CONTAINS]->(si:SastIssue)
OPTIONAL MATCH (repo)-[:CONTAINS]->(fix:Commit)-[:REFERENCES]->(si)
OPTIONAL MATCH (fix)-[:CHANGED]->(:FileVersion)<-[:HAS_VERSION]-(file:File)
WITH repo, app, owner, si, fix, collect(DISTINCT file.name) AS changedFiles
RETURN repo.name AS repository,
       app.name AS application,
       owner.name AS owner,
       si.name AS sastIssue,
       si.date AS issueDate,
       fix.name AS remediationCommit,
       fix.date AS fixDate,
       fix.description AS remediationDescription,
       changedFiles
ORDER BY fixDate DESC, sastIssue
LIMIT 25

tools.name: cve_business_impact
tools.description:
Use for questions about a named CVE code.
Returns impacted libraries or software, applications, business processes, owners and servers.
Use when the user asks where a CVE shows up in the bank landscape or what business capability it can affect.
Parameter cve_code must exactly match CVE.cve_code.

config.template:
MATCH (c:CVE {cve_code: $cve_code})
OPTIONAL MATCH (c)-[:AFFECTS]->(lib:Library)<-[:IMPORTS]-(:File)<-[:CONTAINS]-(:Repository)<-[:HAS_REPO]-(appFromLib:Application)
OPTIONAL MATCH (c)-[:AFFECTS]->(sw:Software)<-[:RUNNING_ON]-(appDirect:Application)
OPTIONAL MATCH (c)-[:AFFECTS]->(sw2:Software)-[:RUNNING_ON]->(:Server)<-[:RUNNING_ON]-(appOnServer:Application)
WITH c, collect(DISTINCT lib.name + ' ' + lib.version) AS libraries,
     collect(DISTINCT sw.name + ' ' + sw.version) + collect(DISTINCT sw2.name + ' ' + sw2.version) AS software,
     collect(DISTINCT appFromLib) + collect(DISTINCT appDirect) + collect(DISTINCT appOnServer) AS rawApps
UNWIND rawApps AS app
OPTIONAL MATCH (app)<-[:USES]-(act:Activity)<-[:CALLS]-(bp:BusinessProcess)
OPTIONAL MATCH (app)<-[:OWNS]-(owner:Owner)
OPTIONAL MATCH (app)-[:RUNNING_ON*1..3]->(srv:Server)
WITH c, libraries, software,
     collect(DISTINCT app.name) AS applications,
     collect(DISTINCT bp.name) AS businessProcesses,
     collect(DISTINCT owner.name) AS owners,
     collect(DISTINCT srv.name) AS servers
RETURN c.cve_code AS cveCode,
       c.title AS title,
       c.severity AS severity,
       c.score AS score,
       [x IN libraries WHERE x IS NOT NULL] AS libraries,
       [x IN software WHERE x IS NOT NULL] AS software,
       [x IN applications WHERE x IS NOT NULL] AS applications,
       [x IN businessProcesses WHERE x IS NOT NULL] AS businessProcesses,
       [x IN owners WHERE x IS NOT NULL] AS owners,
       [x IN servers WHERE x IS NOT NULL] AS servers
LIMIT 10

tools.name: owner_blast_radius
tools.description:
Use for questions about one Owner and everything in their scope.
Returns owned business processes, applications, servers and the associated security signals.
Use when the user asks who is responsible, what an owner controls or how large the blast radius is for a named owner.
Parameter owner_name must exactly match Owner.name.

config.template:
MATCH (o:Owner {name: $owner_name})
OPTIONAL MATCH (o)-[:OWNS]->(bp:BusinessProcess)
OPTIONAL MATCH (o)-[:OWNS]->(app:Application)
OPTIONAL MATCH (o)-[:OWNS]->(srv:Server)
OPTIONAL MATCH (app)-[:HAS_REPO]->(:Repository)-[:CONTAINS]->(si:SastIssue)
OPTIONAL MATCH (app)-[:HAS_REPO]->(:Repository)-[:CONTAINS]->(:File)-[:IMPORTS]->(:Library)<-[:AFFECTS]-(libCve:CVE)
OPTIONAL MATCH (app)-[:RUNNING_ON]->(sw:Software)<-[:AFFECTS]-(runtimeCve1:CVE)
OPTIONAL MATCH (srv)<-[:RUNNING_ON]-(runtimeSw:Software)<-[:AFFECTS]-(runtimeCve2:CVE)
RETURN o.name AS owner,
       o.role AS role,
       collect(DISTINCT bp.name) AS businessProcesses,
       collect(DISTINCT app.name) AS applications,
       collect(DISTINCT srv.name) AS servers,
       count(DISTINCT si) AS sastIssues,
       count(DISTINCT libCve) AS libraryCVEs,
       count(DISTINCT runtimeCve1) + count(DISTINCT runtimeCve2) AS runtimeCVEs
LIMIT 10

parameters.name: owner_name
parameters.description: Name and Surname of a Person (Owner)

tools.name: entrypoint_downstream_impact
tools.description:
Use for questions about a named entry-point server such as bastion or web tier.
Returns downstream servers, applications, business processes and CVEs reachable within the bank network.
Use when the user asks what can be impacted from a server, which business capabilities depend on a server, or how a DMZ node connects to critical assets.
Parameter server_name must exactly match Server.name.

config.template:
MATCH (entry:Server {name: $server_name})
OPTIONAL MATCH (entry)-[:CONNECTED_WITH*1..3]->(srv:Server)
OPTIONAL MATCH (srv)<-[:RUNNING_ON]-(app:Application)
OPTIONAL MATCH (srv)<-[:RUNNING_ON]-(sw:Software)<-[:AFFECTS]-(c:CVE)
OPTIONAL MATCH (app)<-[:USES]-(act:Activity)<-[:CALLS]-(bp:BusinessProcess)
RETURN entry.name AS entryServer,
       collect(DISTINCT srv.name) AS downstreamServers,
       collect(DISTINCT app.name) AS applications,
       collect(DISTINCT bp.name) AS businessProcesses,
       collect(DISTINCT c.cve_code) AS runtimeCVEs
LIMIT 10

tools.name: similar_security_findings
tools.description:
Use for fuzzy security questions about code findings, leak patterns, authorization defects, deserialization, path traversal or logging issues.
Searches semantically similar SAST issues.

tools.name: similar_cve_knowledge
tools.description:
Use for fuzzy vulnerability questions when the user does not know the exact CVE code but describes the flaw, such as log forging, path traversal, remote code execution or authorization bypass.
Searches semantically similar CVEs.
